question.problem:
Find the equation of the tangent line to the polar curve $r=2\theta $ at $\theta =\frac{\pi }{2},$ given that 

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }.
$$
question.worked_solution:
To find the equation of the tangent line to a polar curve at a point $P,$ we follow four steps:

**Step 1**: Calculate the derivative $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}:$

In this case, we're given that

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }.
$$

**Step 2**: Find the slope of the tangent at $P:$

The slope of the tangent line is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ={\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{\theta =\pi /2} \\  & =\frac{(\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{\pi }{2}+\frac{\pi }{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{\pi }{2})}{(\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{\pi }{2}-\frac{\pi }{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{\pi }{2})} \\  & =\frac{(1+\frac{\pi }{2}\cdot 0)}{(0-\frac{\pi }{2}\cdot 1)} \\  & =-\frac{2}{\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Find the Cartesian coordinates of $P:$

We compute the $xy$-coordinates of $P$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =2\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =2\cdot \frac{\pi }{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{\pi }{2} \\  & =0 \\ {y}_{1} & =r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =2\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =2\cdot \frac{\pi }{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{\pi }{2} \\  & =\pi \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of $P$ are $(0,\pi ).$

**Step 4**: Using point-slope form, find the equation of the tangent:

We find the equation of the tangent as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-\pi  & =-\frac{2}{\pi }\cdot (x-0) \\ y & =-\frac{2}{\pi }x+\pi \end{aligned}
$$
